title.narrative: COVID-19: Support for COVID-19 Vaccine Delivery in Mongolia under the Asia Pacific Vaccine Access Facility

description.narrative:
The risk of continued community spread of the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) in Mongolia remains substantial. Since the first case of community transmission was reported on
10 November 2020, several clusters of local transmission have emerged in the capital city and six provinces.
Proposal. The Government of Mongolia officially requested ADB support for securing safe and effective COVID-19 vaccine. The proposed project seeks to provide a loan, through the Asia Pacific Vaccine Access Facility (APVAX) facility, amounting to $40 million to support COVID-19 vaccine delivery in Mongolia.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: COVID-19 vaccines for priority population efficiently procured and delivered Indicator: At least 2,274,838 doses received by the MOH Achievement: 8,397,550 Progress/Status: Eligible vaccines received by MOH. Data source: Ministry of Health, National Communicable Disease Center. Weekly Report on Vaccination Against COVID-19. May 28 - June 3, 2022.
The Government of Mongolia received/ procured in total of 8,397,550 doses of 4 different vaccines. There was a reserve of around 2.3 million doses of COVID-19 vaccines in stock. Thus, the MOH concluded that this output was fully completed. Data Source: Government and project's procurement and quarterly vaccine delivery reports; and MOH quarterly reports Actual value: 8,397,550

Output: COVID-19 vaccines for priority population efficiently procured and delivered Indicator: At least 35 shelters and one-stop service centers catering to victims of gender-based violence receive COVID-19 vaccines for their operational staff members Achievement: 38 Progress/Status: Completed by Q1 2022. All 154 (100%) staff of 38 shelters/one-stop service centers catering to victims of gender-based violence received COVID-19 vaccines. Data Source: Government and project's procurement and quarterly vaccine delivery reports; and MOH quarterly reports

Output: Primary health care services for noncommunicable diseases disrupted by COVID-19 reestablished Indicator: Additional 2,000 cases of rehabilitation services provided by primary health care centers Achievement: 94744 Progress/Status: Overachieved. As of 31 December 2024, in total 94,744 cases (89,758 individuals, out of which 62.2% women) of rehabilitation services were provided by primary health care, financed by the project. This is out of total 181,255 cases (154,021 individuals, out of which 61.3% women) of rehabilitation services, provided by the primary health care annually, nationwide. Source: HIGO annual report 2024; MOH annual report 2024; project annual report, 2024. Data Source: Quarterly and annual statistics and reports from the Health Development Center and the Health Insurance General Office

Output: Awareness on COVID-19 vaccination and delivery enhanced Indicator: At least 3,000 people reached and have enhanced awareness on COVID-19 prevention Achievement: 202831 Progress/Status: Overachieved. As of 31 December 2024, in total 202,831 (67.4% women) people reached and have enhanced awareness on COVID-19, and other communicable and non-communicable diseases, during consultations provided along with rehabilitation services (89,758 individuals, 62.2% women), day care (83,776 individuals, 75.6% women), and home care (29,297 individuals, 60% women), provided by the primary health care, and financed by the project.
Source: HIGO annual report 2024; MOH annual report 2024; project annual report, 2024. Data Source: Quarterly and annual statistics and reports from the Health Development Center and the Health Insurance General Office on home visits by health care workers
Priority population vaccinated against COVID-19 without disruption of primary health care services

Additional 12,000 high-risk individuals (children under 5 years, pregnant women, and older persons) benefited from primary health care home services Achievement: 29297 Progress/Status: Overachieved. As of 31 December 2024, in total 29,297 (60% women) high-risk individuals benefited from home care, provided by primary health care centers and financed by the project, out of total 45,854 (60.9% women) individuals, received home care annually, nationwide. The total number of individuals, benefitted from the project supported home care, include 2,109 (48% girls) children under 5 years; 107 pregnant women; and 18,457 (63.4% women) elderly people over 60 years.
Source: HIGO annual report 2024; MOH annual report 2024; project annual report, 2024. Data Source: MOH and NCCD vaccination coverage reports

Share of population in Mongolia vaccinated against COVID-19 in line with the national immunization strategy and plan increased Achievement: 2,284,250 Progress/Status: Achieved. As of January 2023, 66% (2,284,250 people, out of which 50.9% women) of the total population of Mongolia received two compulsory doses of the effective and safe vaccines against COVID-19 The vaccination campaign conducted in line with the NDVP.
Source. MOH and NCCD reports on vaccination against COVID-19; MOH annual report 2023; project annual report 2023.
Data Sources: Ministry of Health, National Communicable Disease Center. Weekly Report on Vaccination Against COVID-19. Data Source: MOH and NCCD vaccination coverage reports Actual value: 2,284,250
